From e0f3b803d74277677697bdf5b5e4c28766cfbc93 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2010 14:21:13 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] um: fix global timer issue when using CONFIG_NO_HZ

commit 482db6df1746c4fa7d64a2441d4cb2610249c679 upstream.

This fixes a issue which was introduced by fe2cc53e ("uml: track and make
up lost ticks").

timeval_to_ns() returns long long and not int.  Due to that UML's timer
did not work properlt and caused timer freezes.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Acked-by: Pekka Enberg <penberg@kernel.org>
Cc: Jeff Dike <jdike@addtoit.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Gortmaker <paul.gortmaker@windriver.com>

diff --git a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
index dec5678fc17..6e3359d6a83 100644
--- a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
+++ b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
@@ -60,7 +60,7 @@ static inline long long timeval_to_ns(const struct timeval *tv)
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/um/os-Linux/time.c`**
   - The type of the variable `remain` was changed from `int` to `long long` in the `disable_timer` function. This change ensures that the variable can properly hold larger values returned by the `timeval_to_ns()` function, which returns a `long long`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `time.c` addresses a bug related to the handling of timer values in the UML (User Mode Linux) environment. By changing the type of `remain` to `long long`, the code now correctly accommodates the larger range of values that can be produced by the `timeval_to_ns()` function. This fix resolves the timer issues that were causing timer freezes, which were introduced by a previous commit that aimed to track and make up for lost ticks. Thus, the change directly relates to ensuring the proper functioning of the timer system when `CONFIG_NO_HZ` is enabled.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `timeval_to_ns()` function returning a value of type `long long`, while the variable `remain` in the `disable_timer` function was declared as an `int`. This mismatch in data types led to potential overflow issues and incorrect handling of timer values, resulting in timer freezes in the UML environment.

Here is the patch:
 
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
 		       "errno = %d\n", errno);
 
 	remain = timeval_to_ns(&time.it_value);
 	if (remain > max)
 		remain = max;
 
 	return remain;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
remain = timeval_to_ns(&time.it_value);
```
Reason:
The variable `remain` is declared as an `int`, while the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long`. This type mismatch can lead to overflow when large timer values are returned, causing incorrect handling of timer values and resulting in timer freezes in the UML environment.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
```
Reason:
Changing the type of `remain` from `int` to `long long` ensures that it can properly store the value returned by `timeval_to_ns()`, preventing overflow and allowing for correct handling of timer values, thus fixing the timer freeze issue.
